rounds.proof_sketch: For dim=2 kernel: block_size = min(dim1, 1024) = min(256, 1024) = 256. Thread indices (threadIdx.x = row) range from 0 to 255. Original guard: 'if (row >= 256) return' - never triggers since max row=255. Mutated guard: 'if (row > 256) return' - also never triggers since max row=255. The difference only matters at row=dim1=256, which is unreachable.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the boundary check in min_reduction_dim2_kernel from 'row >= dim1' to 'row > dim1'. This would allow thread row=dim1 to execute in the mutant instead of returning early. However, given the fixed input shape [16, 256, 256], we have dim1=256 and block_size=min(256, 1024)=256. CUDA thread indices (threadIdx.x) for a block of size 256 range from 0 to 255. Therefore, no thread ever has row=256. Both the original condition (row >= 256) and mutated condition (row > 256) evaluate to FALSE for all valid thread indices [0-255], making the mutation behaviorally equivalent under this fixed configuration.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed shape [16, 256, 256] because the mutated boundary row=dim1=256 is unreachable - threadIdx.x only reaches 255. Would require changing input shapes to trigger the difference, which violates the testing contract.
rounds.recommendations: When testing boundary guard mutations in CUDA kernels, verify that the mutation affects a reachable boundary. For guards like 'if (idx >= limit) return', the boundary idx=limit is only reachable if the block/grid launch parameters allow indices to reach that value. In this case, block_size exactly equals dim1, making the >= vs > mutation at the boundary unreachable.
